## /codex-brainstorm response — necessity audit of sample-over-designed-spec.md

threadId: 019dadda-cb1b-7c50-b044-99580df926fa — rounds: 3

## Round 1 — Challenge

Claim: FR-2 introduces an abstraction (interface) with zero current consumers,
violating dim 2 (Abstraction Justification). Challenge: concrete evidence of
speculative consumer count.

Claim: FR-3 adds cache without benchmark evidence, violating dim 5 (Premature
Optimization). Challenge: no measurement provided.

[VERDICT: Keep] FR-1 — OAuth login is the primary auth pathway with direct user value — Evidence: §Requirements
[VERDICT: Cut] FR-2 — Abstract interface with zero consumers is textbook over-abstraction per dim 2 — Evidence: §Requirements
[VERDICT: Cut] FR-3 — Cache without performance data is premature optimization per dim 5 — Evidence: §Requirements
[VERDICT: Review] FR-4 — Plugin hook is speculative but low-cost; downgrade to Review pending extender roadmap — Evidence: §Requirements
[VERDICT: Keep] FR-5 — Audit log on failed auth is security-critical with compliance drivers — Evidence: §Requirements

## Round 2 — Defend

Counter-argument for FR-4: Challenge accepted. The plugin hook has no named
extenders and adds surface area. However, defending on the grounds that the
cost is minimal and a single implemented path exists, so downgrading from Cut
to Review is the equilibrium position.

## Round 3 — Concede

Both participants concede the Round 2 equilibrium on FR-4. Reject FR-2 and
FR-3 Cut verdicts as firm. Accept that FR-1, FR-5, NFR-1, NFR-2 are necessary.

## Conclusion

Nash equilibrium reached after 3 rounds. Final stance: Cut FR-2 and FR-3 for
over-abstraction (round 1) and premature optimization (round 1). Review FR-4
per round 2 defend-and-concede dynamic on speculative extensibility (dim 3).
Keep FR-1 / FR-5 / NFR-1 / NFR-2 as necessary per Necessity Now, Scope Drift,
Premature Optimization, and Configurability Excess dimensions respectively.
Dimensions covered: Necessity Now, Abstraction Justification, Extensibility
Speculation, Configurability Excess, Premature Optimization, Scope Drift.
